root.label: Threads and jthread
root.note: A thread handle owns at most one thread and must join or detach it; jthread stops and joins for you.

children.label: Construction
children.note: The callable and arguments are decay-copied in the calling thread, then invoked as rvalues.

children.label: int& parameters
children.note: A plain argument cannot bind to int&; the call is ill-formed without std::ref.

children.label: std::ref
children.note: Passes a reference_wrapper, so the thread sees the original object; it must outlive the use.

children.label: Deferred conversion
children.note: A char array is copied as char*; the std::string parameter is built later, in the new thread.

children.label: Start synchronizes
children.note: The end of the constructor synchronizes with the start of the thread's function.

children.label: Joinable lifecycle
children.note: Joinable from construction until join, detach or move; default-constructed handles are not.

children.label: Destructor terminates
children.note: Destroying or move-assigning over a joinable std::thread calls std::terminate.

children.label: join
children.note: Thread completion synchronizes with join's return; self-join throws resource_deadlock_would_occur.

children.label: detach
children.note: Nothing can wait for it later; using the library after static destruction starts is undefined.

children.label: Exceptions
children.note: Exceptions never cross from one thread to another.

children.label: Escape terminates
children.note: An exception leaving the thread function calls std::terminate; try around join cannot catch it.

children.label: Carry it across
children.note: Catch inside, store a std::exception_ptr, or use a promise or packaged_task.

children.label: std::jthread (C++20)
children.note: Owns a stop_source; the destructor calls request_stop() and then join().

children.label: Token injection
children.note: If the callable takes a stop_token first, jthread passes its own token automatically.

children.label: Cooperative
children.note: Nothing interrupts the thread; it must poll stop_requested or block in a stop-aware wait.

children.label: request_stop
children.note: Returns true only for the call that actually makes the request.

children.label: stop_callback
children.note: Runs in the requesting thread, or at once in its constructor if stop was already requested.

children.label: stop_possible
children.note: False with no stop state, or when no stop_source remains that could still request.

children.label: Identity and hints
children.note: Ids name threads; hardware_concurrency is only advice.

children.label: thread::id
children.note: Default id means no thread; ids are ordered and hashable, and may be reused after a thread ends.

children.label: hardware_concurrency
children.note: Number of hardware thread contexts as a hint; may return 0.

children.label: thread_local
children.note: Each thread has its own instance, destroyed when that thread exits.

children.label: Initialization
children.note: Block scope: first pass in each thread. Namespace scope: may be deferred until first use.

children.label: Destruction
children.note: Reverse construction order at thread exit, completed before join returns.

children.label: Main thread
children.note: Main's thread_local objects are destroyed before any static-storage object.
